questions.subject: Maths
questions.prompt: A triangle has a base of 12 cm and a height of 6 cm. What is its area?

block.label: Quick Recall
block.sub: Four options, one answer — keep it fast

questions.why: Area of a triangle is ½ × base × height, so ½ × 12 × 6 = 36 cm². Don't forget to halve after multiplying.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.prompt: For a cylinder, which part of the formula gives the area of BOTH circular ends together?

block.label: Scrub It
block.sub: Rub out the wrong answers with your finger

questions.why: Each circular end has area πr², and there are two ends, so together they contribute 2πr². Using just πr² only covers one end.

questions.subject: Science
questions.prompt: In an open container, why does the measured mass seem to decrease after burning?
accept: gas is released into the air
questions.why: In an open system, gas produced by the reaction escapes into the air, so the measured mass appears to drop even though mass is still conserved overall.

questions.subject: Science
questions.prompt: What is the name for a solid that suddenly forms when two liquids react?
questions.why: A precipitate is an insoluble solid that forms suddenly when two solutions react together.
